UI Loading

Each UI bundle is stored as a zip that is attached to a release in the GitLab or GitHub repository that hosts your site’s UI project. Here’s how it works.

  1. Antora resolves the latest release of the UI unless specified using the tag key.

  2. It downloads the UI bundle attached to that release.

  3. It extracts this zip file and adds the file contents to the vinyl collection previously described in fetch-content.html.

From this point forward, the pipeline interfaces only with the UI files in the virtual file collection, thus abstracting away the details of the UI’s origin.

The UI bundle is cached inside build after the first time you run Antora. The cached bundle is used automatically on subsequent runs. New UI releases are not picked up automatically.

Fetch a new UI bundle

If you want to force Antora to resolve and download a new UI bundle, you must pass the --skip-theme-cache switch:

$ node generate --skip-theme-cache

The alternative is to remove the build/themes directory, which is where the cache is stored.

Rate limits and personal access tokens

If you fetch the UI often, you might find that you bump into the GitLab or GitHub rate limit. If this happens, you can increase the limit by passing a personal access token when you run Antora:

$ GITHUB_TOKEN=xxxxx node generate --skip-theme-cache
